title: Customer Edge Telemetry Export Contract (PRD - WIP)
summary: Draft PRD describing a configurable telemetry export contract that allows customers running Redwood Private to receive audit logs and operational telemetry at their edge (customer-managed collector) while preserving compliance controls and approval gates.
body:
Context:
- Goal: provide a formal export contract and implementation sketch so regulated customers can operate a customer-managed telemetry collector (on their VPC or on-prem) that receives the minimum necessary logs and metrics from Redwood Private without leaking sensitive data or weakening auditability.

Motivation / Problem Statement:
- Many enterprise customers require that audit logs and operational telemetry be retained within their network boundary or forwarded into their SIEM/Kafka.
- Current ad-hoc mechanisms (SCPs and manual S3 pulls) are brittle, produce inconsistent schemas, and create security gaps.
- We need a predictable, auditable, and configurable contract that: (a) specifies schema, retention hints, filtering rules; (b) enforces approval gates for enabling exports; (c) supports signed manifests and encryption-in-transit; (d) provides backpressure and proof-of-delivery semantics.

Key user stories:
- Security/compliance officer: "I must be able to approve telemetry exports and limit exported fields to exclude PII or customer prompt payloads."
- Platform engineer: "I want a stable contract so my SIEM ingestion pipelines don't break with each release."
- SRE: "I need proof that logs were delivered within SLA windows and a fallback if the collector is unreachable."

Scope (what in / out):
- In scope: audit logs (auth, admin actions, rollouts, operator API calls), control-plane operational metrics (request latency, error counts), delivery contract (TLS + mTLS, signed manifests, sequence numbers), export filters and redaction rules, approval gating flow in Console, telemetry compliance matrix (SOC2/GDPR mapping).
- Out of scope (for this PRD): high-volume token-level traces, application-level customer content replication, long-term archival UI (we will rely on customers pulling and retaining on their side).

Design overview:
1) Export endpoint model:
   - Customer deploys an "edge collector" (open-source agent) in their VPC or on-prem. Collector exposes an mTLS endpoint with mutually-authenticated certs.
   - Redwood control plane establishes outbound connection to collector using outbound-only IP ranges and negotiates a per-customer export session.

2) Contract artifacts:
   - Schema v1 (JSON Lines): stable fields list for logs and metrics, with explicit redaction markers.
   - Signed export manifest: a small JSON document signed by Redwood's export authority listing sequence ranges, schema version, and SHA256 digest of each batch.
   - Delivery acknowledgement: collector returns a signed ACK per-batch; Redwood stores ACK receipts for 90 days.

3) Approval gates & UX:
   - Console: new "Telemetry Exports" page under Private > Integrations. Admins can request export to a target collector.
   - Two-step approval: (1) Customer admin registers collector endpoint and certificate (self-serve); (2) Security approver toggles "Approve exporter" which flips a tenant-level flag and records audit event.
   - Default state: exports disabled. A history of approvals is retained and surfaced in rollout audit.

4) Redaction and filtering:
   - Predicate-based filters: allow inclusion/exclusion rules per-log-type.
   - Redaction templates: pre-built patterns to strip prompt text, embeddings payloads, or headers.
   - Validation: dry-run mode to show sample outputs in Console before enabling.

5) Reliability & backpressure:
   - Delivery semantics: at-least-once with sequence numbers and idempotency keys.
   - Buffering: Redwood queues batches up to configured tenant quota; if collector unreachable for > X hours, alert and pause exports (fail-closed option available for high-compliance tenants).
   - Rollback: on pause, exports are suspended and an internal incident is opened; manual resume requires approver.

6) Security and encryption:
   - Mandatory mTLS + token rotation cadence (90 days).
   - Option to use customer-managed KMS for envelope encryption of sensitive payloads.
   - Signed manifests to prove provenance for audits.

Compliance mapping:
- SOC2: record of approvals, retention of ACK receipts, manifest signatures.
- GDPR: support field-level pseudonymization and export consent toggles.
- PCI: recommend fail-closed; exclude any sensitive payment content via filters.

Operational considerations:
- Cost: increased egress and storage on customer side; outline a metered export feature for Hosted -> Private transition assistance.
- Observability: Redwood will provide per-export metrics (bytes/sec, last-ack, fail_count) in Console and via the existing API.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Alpha (Q1): small set of pilot customers; manual approvals via SE; basic schema + signed manifests.
- Beta (Q2): Console UX, dry-run mode, filters, ACK receipts retention.
- GA (Q3): full production SLAs, KMS integrations, fail-closed option.

Open questions / risks:
- Schema churn: how to manage breaking changes? Propose a strict semantic version and 12-month runway for deprecations.
- Data minimization: what's our default for prompt retention in logs? Recommend default redaction of prompt text unless explicitly approved.
- Network egress constraints for air-gapped customers: need an alternate transfer mode (SFTP bundle pick-up) — design stubbed but not implemented here.

Implementation notes / tech dependencies:
- Engineering: edge-collector repo changes, export queue and signing service, Console frontend + RBAC hooks.
- Security: review key lifecycle, HSM/KMS integration, manifest signing key custody.
- SRE: add delivery SLAs, incident playbooks for export outages.

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- Pilot customers can register collector and receive schema v1 logs over mTLS.
- Console shows dry-run sample for granted filters.
- Signed manifests and ACK receipts are being stored and retrievable for 90 days.
- Approval events recorded in tenant audit log with approver identity.

Next steps (owners):
- Draft schema v1 (Marco) — due 2025-11-21
- Edge collector mTLS handshake spec (Liang) — due 2025-11-28
- Console approval flow mocks (Priya) — due 2025-11-24
- Compliance review draft (Tom) — due 2025-12-05

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an early draft intended to capture product intent and interfaces. Please comment inline in Confluence link provided in linked_artifacts.
- If you have a customer example that requires a different delivery mode (SFTP/pull), add a note and tag @Priya.
